newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weaker, MidEast premiums tumble.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weaker, MidEast premiums tumble.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower on Wednesday, with Middle East grades leading the way down as their premiums took a dive.
In a raft of deals, premiums for light Middle East grades slipped into the late teens to mid 20s from the early 30s Tuesday, while Qatar Marine fell to QGPC +15 cents, from +20.
A major, seeing little demand but good supply, was bidding QGPC -20 cents for Qatar Marine.
Murban was traded at ADNOC +18 cents after +30 on Tuesday, while Umm Shaif was said traded at ADNOC +34 cents, although traders said this was too high to have been a recent deal.
Trades were talked on Oman as low as MPM +6 cents, with a deals at MPM +8 and +9 cents confirmed. The MPM +6 cent deals involved Japanese traders and refiners, traders said.
The latest lows have taken another lump off the Oman premium, which was last traded at MPM +10 cents. At the start of March trading, deals were seen at MPM +27 cents.
Traders said plunging product prices and cuts in production runs at Singapore refineries were taking their toll on premiums.
Bangchak's March buying tender closes later on Wednesday and will provide the next price idea from the market for Oman and other Middle East grades.
A major seller of Oman was heard selling Oman at both MPM +9 cents and +10 cents, although at least one of the deals was said to be a partial cargo.
Brent and Dubai paper swaps were mostly steady from a day earlier with April and May all trading around $2.00 per barrel.
March/April and April/May Dubai was quoted around 35 cents, reflecting overnight deals at that level.
Regional grades were steady with most February grades placed, although Bach Ho was on offer traders said.
